questions.q: What makes AI red-teaming a formal assessment practice rather than freeform attacking?
options: It requires no written scope, since AI systems are tested informally by design
It only ever happens accidentally, when a user stumbles into a jailbreak
It is run without any involvement from the team that owns the system
It runs under a defined scope, written authorization, a time-boxed window, and a formal report, the same discipline as a penetration test
questions.explain: AI red-teaming mirrors penetration-testing methodology: rules of engagement, authorization from the risk owner, a bounded test window, and a reported, reproducible set of findings.

questions.q: A red-team test case checking whether a model can be pushed into producing content its own policy should block is testing for which category covered earlier in this course?
options: Harmful-output generation
Terraform state drift
SQL injection against a relational database
DNS cache poisoning
questions.explain: This is the harmful-output-generation category (Chapters 2 and 5): adversarial phrasing or crafted input used to bypass the system's own content policy.

questions.q: What is MITRE ATLAS, and how is it used in AI red-teaming?
options: A proprietary scanner sold exclusively by Microsoft for internal use only
A published, MITRE-maintained catalog of real adversary tactics and techniques against machine learning systems, used to build test plans from documented attacker behavior
A mapping tool used only for cloud network topology diagrams
A certification exam for AI red-team practitioners
questions.explain: MITRE ATLAS mirrors the structure of MITRE ATT&CK but catalogs tactics and techniques specific to attacking ML systems, giving teams a documented, real-world basis for test design.

questions.q: Why do rules of engagement specify an in-scope system, a time-boxed window, and written authorization before testing begins?
options: Because those details are purely ceremonial and have no bearing on whether testing is authorized
Because AI systems cannot be tested without first disabling all of their safety features
Because that scoping and authorization is exactly what distinguishes an authorized assessment from unauthorized attacking
Because they are required only when the system being tested has no production traffic
questions.explain: The written scope and authorization are what make the activity a sanctioned assessment rather than an attack — the same requirement that governs authorized penetration testing.

questions.q: Which step comes last in the AI red-team engagement lifecycle described in this lesson?
options: Scoping and authorization
Executing test cases and logging prompts and responses
Retesting to confirm a reported finding is actually fixed
Designing test cases from frameworks like MITRE ATLAS
questions.explain: The lifecycle runs scope and authorize, then threat-informed test design, then execution and logging, then reporting, and finally retest — confirming the fix actually closes the finding rather than just changing the original test's outcome.
